rv.q: The production confidently walks this tonal line between sincerity and satire, and the play never settles for easy cynicism.
This is innovative theatre, shining with intelligence, which brings richness to our cultural tussle with the problem of ancient statues and their rightful place in the world.
It’s a hard thing to pin down, other than to say that it really is way too long, and succeeds in its restless breadth where it doesn’t in giving us depth.
Tan has written a play that feels at once sweeping in scope and completely nuanced.
This highly entertaining political satire of topical issues encourages us to care about and applaud those fighting for the return of objects Britain has stolen from other countries.
Nevertheless, Scenes of a Repatriation is a bold, imaginative piece of theatre.
This is still a fine and important contribution to a growing debate, and not one confined to museology.
It is exactly the kind of play you want the Royal Court to present in this space.
The writing is insightful and concise, rendering many scenes simultaneously touching, shocking and funny.

Somehow as intellectually accessible as it is challenging, and as willing to allow interpretation as it is concrete in the points it raises, Scenes from a Repatriation gives voice to many continually pressing concerns both at home and overseas.
This is a powerful, thought-provoking, and educational theatrical experience.
It is not entirely successful, but when it works it works well.
This high-octane production demonstrates how antiquities can be weaponised in displays of power, and questions who truly owns cultural artefacts.
All those attempts carry a precise and sharp perspective, while they don’t feel forced, out of context, or pandering to a Western gaze through superficial critique of the CCP.

cn.t: Critics praise Joel Tan's ambitious, genre-bending exploration of cultural repatriation as powerful and original, with inventive staging that brings intellectual heft to the British Museum debate, though some find its fragmented structure uneven.
